text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- Bosnia elections: Some 70 percent of the voters went to the polls, preliminary results to be made public today.
- War invalids' Zagreb protest rally: Defence Minister Susak pledges to put into action all promises to them by president Tudjman.
- Hunger strike because of the Zagreb crisis. A member of the Croatian Independent Democrats (HND) party, Josip Kokic is on a hunger strike in protest of the Zagreb crisis still not being resolved.
- The home of a Croatian intelectual blown up in Bugojno. The incident threatened to hamper the elections in the area.
- What are the ways of improving cattle breeding? In the first six months of 1996 Croatia has imported $109 million dollars worth of meet products and has expored only $65 million.
- (The Defence Minister Gojko) Susak and myself are not trying to topple (Prime Minister Zlatko) Matesa, says in an interview Parliament's deputy speaker Vladimir Seks.

- Due to bad investments, the Croats are losing billions of German marks, claims in an interview Stefan Buchberger, the director of the Munich branch of AWD, the largest independent European financial and economic consultancy. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
